newsitem.title: UK: Arson suspected at UK utility chief's home.
newsitem.headline: Arson suspected at UK utility chief's home.

text.p: Fire broke out on Saturday at the home of the chairman of Britain's water and electricity giant United Utilities Plc and police said they were treating it as arson.
The blaze in the kitchen of the north-western England home of Sir Desmond Pitcher caused only minor damage and no injuries. The house was unoccupied at the time.
An anonymous call to a local newspaper said the house had been fire-bombed. The caller added; "Three of the fat cats and all of the fat cats are terrorist targets."
Pitcher is one of a number of executives at Britain's recently privatised utilities companies who have been criticised for taking huge pay rises for running what were effectively monopoly industries.
Shareholders last year rejected an incentive scheme offering directors an extra 87 percent on their salaries. Pitcher was himself attacked as a "fat cat".
Police said Pitcher's home and its grounds had been sealed off for investigation.
"The fire is being treated as suspicious and a criminal investigation has commenced," said a police spokesman.
